title: The Iron Plough Farmers Feared, and the Barren Land at Kundal Road
conflicts: Plough year 1903 (company) vs 1905 (Business Today): both given. Belgaum eviction 1908 (Business Today) vs January 1910 (All About Belgaum): both given. Raja of Aundh's loan 10,000 rupees (1969 P&T stamp folder, All About Belgaum) vs 17,000 (Wikipedia): folder figure used and attributed. Who opened the 1888 shop (Ramchandrarao per Business Today, Laxmanrao per folder and company): story says the family firm, run at first by Ramchandrarao.
notes: Arc changed from change-of-direction to setback: the episode is the forced move from Belgaum and the March 1910 restart with 25 workers; the bicycles-to-ploughs shift is background. Sources are thinner than ideal: Business Today (2011) is the main independent account, plus a transcription of the 1969 P&T stamp folder, the group's legacy page and a local Belgaum site; Economic Times, Indian Express and Business Standard pieces load for the verifier but could not be read here. No first-person account of Laxmanrao was found, so no thoughts are attributed. Stance affirms (Hesiod's hundred timbers to a waggon).
